sentences.text: Ichthyodectes was an extinct genus of marine ray-finned fish belonging to the ichthyodectid family.
It is classified in the superorder Osteoglossomorpha, order Ichthyodectiformes, and family Ichthyodectidae.
The species Ichthyodectes ctenodon was found in formations across Canada, the United States, and England.
Fossil evidence of a stomach containing a smaller fish confirms that Ichthyodectes had a piscivorous diet.
A notable complete skeleton of Ichthyodectes ctenodon was officially described in 2010 after being collected by Charles H. Sternberg prior to 1919.
Ichthyodectes lived from the Cenomanian to the Campanian stages, between 100.5 and 72.2 million years ago.
Recent analyses suggest that only two species can be confidently placed in the genus Ichthyodectes, with others being synonymous or belonging to different genera.
